tactile stimulation outside of the receptive field (RF), but within the hand, can suppress the ongoing discharge of neurons in primary somosensory cortex.
tactile stimulation can suppress the spontaneous activity of neurons recorded in the hand representation in somatosensorsory cortex of awake primates.
tactile stimulation outside of a neuron's excitatory RF can suppress spontaneous firing in the somatosensory cortical neurons of awake and anesthesized New World monkeys and galagos.

the mechanisms of tactile suppression of neuronal responses in somatosensary cortex.

suppression is a common response property of neurons in the primary somatosensary cortex of primates.

suppression of spontaneous firing is a common response to tactile stimuli on skin sites outside of the excitant RF of neurons in primary somatic sensory cortex.

tactile stimulation can suppress the spontaneous activity of neurons within the somatosensory representation of the hand.
the tactile sensory cortex is a highly dynamic structure, with neurons responding in a variety of ways to stimulation across the skin surface.
neurons in primary sensory cortex are not only responsive to tactile stimuli, but also can be inhibited by tactile stimuli outside of the RF.
